newsitem.title: GERMANY: BOE's Davies - U.K. policy to deliver convergence.
newsitem.headline: BOE's Davies - U.K. policy to deliver convergence.

text.p: Bank of England Deputy Governor Howard Davies said on Friday that U.K. policies were likely to deliver fiscal convergence in 1997.

"The Chancellor of the Exchequer has said that he is sympathetic in principle to the idea of a single currency for the whole of the European Union, as long as it is well-founded in sustainable convergence.
"And we can say that the U.K.'s policies are likely to deliver fiscal convergence this year," he said in the text of speech to be delivered at a payments conference in Frankfurt.
Davies also said that the operational independence newly granted to the Bank of England did not make it "immediately Maastricht compatible".
"Nor do I wish to imply that the U.K. is likely to join in 1999. The prime minister has said it is highly unlikely," he added.

"What is important to note, though, is that there is no question of the United Kingdom pursuing a destructive, inflationary monetary policy outside the euro zone, if that is where we find ourselves in 1999," he said.

Davies said the Bank of England expected to be given an inflation target which would be at least as tight as the 2.5 percent or less regime in which it had operated in recent years and would do its best to meet that.
"So the concerns which have been expressed about the potential behaviour of the U.K. as a pre-in country are, I think, wide of the mark (or should I now say, wide of the euro?)," Davies said.
He declined to comment on today's rise in the interest rate, referring reporters to the statement issued by the Bank of England on the 1/4 point rate increase.

He also declined comment on moves by the new French government to seek renegotiation of the stability pact, the agreement between European countries aimed at ensuring fiscal discipline within a single currency zone.
"I think you should ask that in French," he quipped.
